source.title: mini-vec2vec: Scaling Universal Geometry Alignment with Linear Transformations

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether text embedding spaces from different models can be aligned by a learned linear map, using held-out paired retrieval accuracy and rank. This is a conceptual test of interchangeable representations, not a scale sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cosine similarity at Initial, Refine-1, and Refine-2 stages, but leaves those values out: the authors caution that cosine is misleading in this setup, and the table’s top-1 and rank metrics directly report the held-out alignment outcome. The vec2vec comparison numbers are reported from Jha et al. (2025), not independently produced here, so they are not cataloged as results.
record.test_reason: The study learns an orthogonal linear map between five independently trained text-embedding models without paired training data. It evaluates the map by held-out retrieval (top-1, average rank), which directly tests V4's 'simple linear map, even without paired data' clause.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author concludes that a cheap linear, non-adversarial unsupervised method matches or exceeds vec2vec at aligning text embedding spaces. He calls this further strong empirical evidence for Universal Geometry and also notes security implications for embedding leakage.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsupervised cluster/anchor matching, Procrustes fitting, and iterative refinement to learn a linear orthogonal map between text embedding spaces; it is not a direct reproduction of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or the original Convergent Learning method.
record.method_sensitivity: The gtr ↔ gte pair uses c = 30 clusters rather than c = 20 to address suboptimal convergence. The paper reports qualitative hyperparameter trends: more anchor runs reduce failures; larger sampling rates and moderate neighbor counts can help; very large neighbor counts may hurt; and the effect of α on cosine need not translate to better rank or top-1. It says a rigorous hyperparameter analysis was not performed.
record.problems: No null controls. Only five text embedding models are tested, on one dataset distribution; the method is evaluated over three runs and a single evaluation set. Top-1 standard deviations are not provided. The paper says the hyperparameter observations were not rigorously analyzed, and the gtr ↔ gte direction has rarer failure modes.
record.rows_left_out: Left out the Initial, Refine-1, and Refine-2 mean cosine values in Table 1, because the authors caution that cosine is misleading in this setup and the included retrieval metrics directly test alignment quality. Also omitted vec2vec comparison values in Table 1 because they are reported from Jha et al. (2025), rather than generated as this study’s own results.

untested.parts: Stitching layers, supervised maps, relative representations as a standalone mapping, non-text modalities, models well above about 300M parameters, and out-of-distribution data (source and target sentences both come from Natural Questions). Contrary to the record, alignment without paired data IS tested: training sentences do not overlap and no pairs are used for fitting.
No sweep over model size or capability. All models are 109M–278M.
No seed comparisons within one architecture.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits are compared.
No variation of similarity metric or input distribution.
No test of plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause. Cosine after alignment (0.49–0.71) is reported but called misleading by the author.

missing.what: Failure-mode results: gtr↔gte converges suboptimally at c=20; residual gtr→gte failures give about 90% top-1 and rank 5–10. Not quantified per run.

record.verdict_notes: Row values match Table 1. Minor correction: Table 1 does report top-1 SD (0.00), contrary to the rows' notes. The chance baseline for top-1 is about 1/8192, so 'baseline not stated' could be filled from the setup. Leaving out the vec2vec values (cited from Jha et al.) and the cosine values is appropriate. Caveats: all models are small BERT/T5/RoBERTa encoders; there are no null or supervised-ceiling controls; hyperparameter robustness claims are informal (Appendix B).

versions.untested_parts: No sweep relating model size or capability to alignment; no test that alignment rises with scale.
Uses text embedding models, not paired vision and language models or image-caption representations.
Does not compare seeds or shared features/subspaces within one architecture.

Tests unsupervised linear alignment for text embedding models on Natural Questions. It does not test stitching, relative representations as a standalone mapping method, or alignment without paired evaluation examples.
Does not identify or compare interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Does not systematically vary the similarity metric, its settings, or input distribution to test metric or data dependence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete.

relationships.display_finding: All 20 directed pairs achieved top-1 retrieval 0.96–1.00 and average rank 1.00–1.10 over 8,192 held-out sentences, with standard deviation 0.00 across three runs.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: All 20 directed pairs among granite, gtr, gte, stella and e5 on Natural Questions, with an unsupervised orthogonal map
source_check.reason: Table 1 supports V4: top-1 0.96–1.00 and average rank 1.00–1.10 on 8192 held-out sentences, with reported SDs rounding to 0.00 across 3 runs. The map description needs qualification: orthogonality is enforced softly through smoothing, and gtr↔gte uses c=30.

relationships.condition: gtr ↔ gte pair under the default c=20 clusters
relationships.reason: Per the text (§4, §5), c=20 often converges suboptimally for this pair. Even at c=30, gtr→gte still fails occasionally (about 90% top-1, rank 5–10). The near-perfect rows r15, r16, r19 and r20 depend on that tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Using 20 clusters often converged suboptimally; even with 30, gtr→gte occasionally reached only about 90% top-1 with ranks 5–10.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: gtr ↔ gte pair under the default c=20 clusters
source_check.reason: §4 explicitly reports frequent suboptimal convergence at c=20 for this pair; r15, r16, r19 and r20 instead report c=30. §5 reports rarer remaining gtr→gte failures, approximately 90% top-1 and average rank 5–10. These limitations are stated in the text rather than quantified by the cited successful rows.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: All 20 directed pairs among granite, gtr, gte, stella and e5 on Natural Questions, with an unsupervised orthogonal map
labels.reason: Table 1 supports V4: top-1 0.96–1.00 and average rank 1.00–1.10 on 8192 held-out sentences, with reported SDs rounding to 0.00 across 3 runs. The map description needs qualification: orthogonality is enforced softly through smoothing, and gtr↔gte uses c=30.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: gtr ↔ gte pair under the default c=20 clusters
labels.reason: §4 explicitly reports frequent suboptimal convergence at c=20 for this pair; r15, r16, r19 and r20 instead report c=30. §5 reports rarer remaining gtr→gte failures, approximately 90% top-1 and average rank 5–10. These limitations are stated in the text rather than quantified by the cited successful rows.

relation.reason: Its own held-out retrieval results directly test V4's simple linear mapping without paired training data.

tranche.reason: The study tests unpaired interchangeability using a different alignment method: cluster matching, linear Procrustes fitting and iterative refinement, evaluated by held-out retrieval.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v4 dated 17 February 2026; orthogonality is relaxed through exponentially smoothed matrices. Table 1's vec2vec comparators come from the earlier paper: its single-run/eight-evaluation-set protocol differs from mini-vec2vec's three-run/single-evaluation-set protocol.
